title: Slim client dependency footprint and retire compatibility shims
creator: Maya Sanchez
description: Audit and reduce the transitive dependency surface for Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and remove the compatibility shims that prolong confusing API behavior. Goals: 1) shrink install/bundle size and improve cold-start for serverless consumers, 2) finish pydantic v1->v2 migration in the Python SDK and remove model transformation shims, 3) replace node-fetch polyfills with undici in the JS SDK and drop the legacy fetch shim, 4) bump Go modules to go1.21 and upgrade grpc/opentelemetry stacks used by the SDK and examples. Additionally, identify deprecated public fields in the API surface (compat_response, legacy_callbacks) and publish a deprecation schedule with automated warnings and a one-release compatibility shim before full removal.
acceptance_criteria:
- Python SDK: pydantic v2 is default, no runtime warnings in conformance suite; dependency set reduced by at least 3 packages (transitive).
- JS SDK: undici used in Node bundles; bundle size reduced and CI matrix green on Node 18/20.
- Go SDK: module proxies updated, builds succeed with go1.21, no lint failures.
- Deprecation: 'compat_response' and 'legacy_callbacks' produce user-facing deprecation warnings for 2 weeks after canary, documented in changelog, and removed in the follow-up release.
- New CI job 'compat-smoke' runs consumer conformance tests against both old and new shims and is green before rollout.
implementation_notes:
1) Run dependency audit across all SDKs and lockfiles; create minimal bump PRs per package group.
2) Python: migrate model marshaling tests to pydantic v2, add adapter layer with lifecycle: deprecation-warning -> shim -> removal. Pin httpx to latest stable and drop requests if not used.
3) JS: replace node-fetch usage in runtime adapter with undici, remove fetch polyfill, update bundling and test matrix. Add ESM/CJS compatibility check.
4) Go: update go.mod to 1.21, upgrade github.com/grpc/grpc-go and go.opentelemetry.io/otel to latest compatible minors, run go vet/gofmt.
5) Add telemetry counters for deprecation warning hits and error spikes.
6) Coordinate with docs and support to notify customers; prepare migration guide snippets and decorators for simple client upgrades.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): merge SDK PRs behind feature flags; publish canary packages (pythonrc/alpha, @redwood/sdk@next-canary, go pre-release). Run compat-smoke pipeline against top-10 internal consumer repos.
- Phase 2 (beta): enable deprecation warnings by default for one week; collect telemetry and customer feedback.
- Phase 3 (general): remove compatibility shims and publish stable releases; update docs and changelogs.
- Phase 4: post-release monitoring for 2 weeks; rollback if error rates exceed thresholds.
rollback_plan:
- If canary fails: revert feature flag and publish previous package.
- If beta shows increased errors from a specific dependency: pin to previous minor and release a hotfix.
- If full removal causes customer outages: reintroduce shim in a patch release and open customer-facing support playbook.
qa_tests:
- Unit + integration suites run on python3.10/3.11/3.12 for Python SDK.
- JS SDK tests on Node 16/18/20 and browsers where applicable.
- Go SDK builds and examples validated on go1.20 and go1.21.
- End-to-end conformance against internal reference app and two external customer testbeds.
- Smoke test: ensure no 5xx increase and token-latency tail (<95th) regressions >10%.
